symbols.summary: A superclass for all contact media - ways to contact an entity represented by a Contact instance. Some of the subclasses of this class (the various kinds of telephone numbers and postal addresses) have been inspired by the values of the TYPE parameter of ADR and TEL properties defined in RFC 2426 sec. 3.2.1. and 3.3.1 respectively. Each value is represented by an appropriate subclass with two major exceptions TYPE=home and TYPE=work. They are to be expressed by the roles these contact media are attached to i.e. contact media with TYPE=home parameter are to be attached to the default role (nco:Contact or nco:PersonContact), whereas media with TYPE=work parameter should be attached to nco:Affiliation or nco:OrganizationContact.

symbols.name: nfo:FileDataObject
symbols.summary: A resource containing a finite sequence of bytes with arbitrary information, that is available to a computer program and is usually based on some kind of durable storage. A file is durable in the sense that it remains available for programs to use after the current program has finished.

symbols.name: nfo:FileHash
symbols.summary: A fingerprint of the file, generated by some hashing function.

symbols.name: nfo:Filesystem
symbols.summary: A filesystem. Examples of filesystems include hard disk partitions, removable media, but also images thereof stored in files.

symbols.name: nfo:FilesystemImage
symbols.summary: An image of a filesystem. Instances of this class may include CD images, DVD images or hard disk partition images created by various pieces of software (e.g. Norton Ghost)

symbols.name: nfo:Folder
symbols.summary: A folder/directory. Examples of folders include folders on a filesystem and message folders in a mailbox.

symbols.name: nfo:Font
symbols.summary: A font.

symbols.name: nfo:GameImage
symbols.summary: A game image. This is a Tracker extension

symbols.name: nfo:HardDiskPartition
symbols.summary: A partition on a hard disk

symbols.name: nfo:HelpDocument
symbols.summary: User guides and similar to assist the user

symbols.name: nfo:HtmlDocument
symbols.summary: A HTML document, may contain links to other files.

symbols.name: nfo:Icon
symbols.summary: An Icon (regardless of whether it's a raster or a vector icon. A resource representing an icon could have two types (Icon and Raster, or Icon and Vector) if required.

symbols.name: nfo:Image
symbols.summary: A file containing an image.

symbols.name: nfo:ImageCategory
symbols.summary: A image category

symbols.name: nfo:Media
symbols.summary: A piece of media content. This class may be used to express complex media containers with many streams of various media content (both aural and visual).

symbols.name: nfo:MediaFileListEntry
symbols.summary: A single node in the list of media files contained within an MediaList instance. This class is intended to provide a type all those links have. In valid NRL untyped resources cannot be linked. There are no properties defined for this class but the application may expect rdf:first and rdf:last links. The former points to the DataObject instance, interpreted as Media the latter points at another MediaFileListEntr. At the end of the list there is a link to rdf:nil.

symbols.name: nfo:MediaList
symbols.summary: A file containing a list of media files.e.g. a playlist

symbols.name: nfo:MediaStream
symbols.summary: A stream of multimedia content, usually contained within a media container such as a movie (containing both audio and video) or a DVD (possibly containing many streams of audio and video). Most common interpretations for such a DataObject include Audio and Video.

symbols.name: nfo:MindMap
symbols.summary: A MindMap, created by a mind-mapping utility. Examples might include FreeMind or mind mapper.

symbols.name: nfo:Note
symbols.summary: Usually small document with snippets, reminders or frequenly used content.

symbols.name: nfo:OperatingSystem
symbols.summary: An OperatingSystem

symbols.name: nfo:Orientation
symbols.summary: Orientation enum

symbols.name: nfo:PaginatedTextDocument
symbols.summary: A file containing a text document, that is unambiguously divided into pages. Examples might include PDF, DOC, PS', DVI etc.

symbols.name: nfo:PlainTextDocument
symbols.summary: A file containing plain text (ASCII, Unicode or other encodings). Examples may include TXT, HTML, XML, program source code etc.

symbols.name: nfo:Presentation
symbols.summary: A Presentation made by some presentation software (Corel Presentations, OpenOffice Impress, MS Powerpoint etc.)

symbols.name: nfo:RasterImage
symbols.summary: A raster image.

symbols.name: nfo:RegionOfInterest
symbols.summary: Area on an image with relevant content. Following the spec in http://www.metadataworkinggroup.org

symbols.name: nfo:RegionOfInterestContent
symbols.summary: Content in the area. There is a predefined set of contents in the spec: http://www.metadataworkinggroup.org

symbols.name: nfo:RemoteDataObject
symbols.summary: A file data object stored at a remote location. Don't confuse this class with a RemotePortAddress. This one applies to a particular resource, RemotePortAddress applies to an address, that can have various interpretations.

symbols.name: nfo:RemotePortAddress
symbols.summary: An address specifying a remote host and port. Such an address can be interpreted in many ways (examples of such interpretations include mailboxes, websites, remote calendars or filesystems), depending on an interpretation, various kinds of data may be extracted from such an address.

symbols.name: nfo:Software
symbols.summary: A piece of software. Examples may include applications and the operating system. This interpretation most commonly applies to SoftwareItems.

symbols.name: nfo:SoftwareApplication
symbols.summary: An application

symbols.name: nfo:SoftwareCategory
symbols.summary: A software category

symbols.name: nfo:SoftwareItem
symbols.summary: A DataObject representing a piece of software. Examples of interpretations of a SoftwareItem include an Application and an OperatingSystem.

symbols.name: nfo:SoftwareService
symbols.summary: A service published by a piece of software, either by an operating system or an application. Examples of such services may include calendar, addresbook and mailbox managed by a PIM application. This category is introduced to distinguish between data available directly from the applications (Via some Interprocess Communication Mechanisms) and data available from files on a disk. In either case both DataObjects would receive a similar interpretation (e.g. a Mailbox) and wouldn't differ on the content level.

symbols.name: nfo:SourceCode
symbols.summary: Code in a compilable or interpreted programming language.

symbols.name: nfo:Spreadsheet
symbols.summary: A spreadsheet, created by a spreadsheet application. Examples might include Gnumeric, OpenOffice Calc or MS Excel.

symbols.name: nfo:TextDocument
symbols.summary: A text document

symbols.name: nfo:Trash
symbols.summary: Represents a container for deleted files, a feature common in modern operating systems.

symbols.name: nfo:VectorImage
symbols.summary: A vector image (e.g. SVG)

symbols.name: nfo:Video
symbols.summary: A video file.

symbols.name: nfo:Visual
symbols.summary: File containing visual content.

symbols.name: nfo:WebHistory
symbols.summary: A web history entry

symbols.name: nfo:Website
symbols.summary: A website, usually a container for remote resources, that may be interpreted as HTMLDocuments, images or other types of content.

symbols.name: nfo:aspectRatio
symbols.summary: Visual content aspect ratio. (Width divided by Height)

symbols.name: nfo:audioOffset
symbols.summary: Specifies the start offset of this resource within a larger file, such as a single song within a recording of a radio broadcast or a CD rip.

symbols.name: nfo:averageAudioBitrate
symbols.summary: The average overall bitrate of a media container. (i.e. the size of the piece of media in bits, divided by it's duration expressed in seconds).

symbols.name: nfo:averageBitrate
symbols.summary: The average overall bitrate of a media container. (i.e. the size of the piece of media in bits, divided by it's duration expressed in seconds).

symbols.name: nfo:averageVideoBitrate
symbols.summary: The average overall bitrate of a media container. (i.e. the size of the piece of media in bits, divided by it's duration expressed in seconds).

symbols.name: nfo:belongsToContainer
symbols.summary: Models the containment relations between Files and Folders (or CompressedFiles).

symbols.name: nfo:bitDepth
symbols.summary: A common superproperty for all properties signifying the amount of bits for an atomic unit of data. Examples of subproperties may include bitsPerSample and bitsPerPixel

symbols.name: nfo:bitrateType
symbols.summary: The type of the bitrate. Examples may include CBR and VBR.

symbols.name: nfo:bitsPerSample
symbols.summary: Amount of bits in each audio sample.

symbols.name: nfo:bookmarks
symbols.summary: The address of the linked object. Usually a web URL.

symbols.name: nfo:channels
symbols.summary: Number of channels. This property is to be used directly if no detailed information is necessary. Otherwise use more detailed subproperties.

symbols.name: nfo:characterCount
symbols.summary: The amount of characters in the document.

symbols.name: nfo:characterPosition
symbols.summary: Character position of the bookmark

symbols.name: nfo:codec
symbols.summary: The name of the codec necessary to decode a piece of media.

symbols.name: nfo:colorDepth
symbols.summary: Amount of bits used to express the color of each pixel.

symbols.name: nfo:commentCharacterCount
symbols.summary: The amount of character in comments i.e. characters ignored by the compiler/interpreter.

symbols.name: nfo:compressionType
symbols.summary: The type of the compression. Values include, lossy and lossless.

symbols.name: nfo:conflicts
symbols.summary: States that a piece of software is in conflict with another piece of software.

symbols.name: nfo:containsBookmark
symbols.summary: The folder contains a bookmark.

symbols.name: nfo:containsBookmarkFolder
symbols.summary: The folder contains a bookmark folder.

symbols.name: nfo:count
symbols.summary: A common superproperty for all properties signifying the amount of atomic media data units. Examples of subproperties may include sampleCount and frameCount.

symbols.name: nfo:definesClass
symbols.summary: Name of a class defined in the source code file.

symbols.name: nfo:definesFunction
symbols.summary: A name of a function/method defined in the given source code file.

symbols.name: nfo:definesGlobalVariable
symbols.summary: Name of a global variable defined within the source code file.

symbols.name: nfo:deletionDate
symbols.summary: The date and time of the deletion.

symbols.name: nfo:depiction
symbols.summary: Relates an information element to an image which depicts said element.

symbols.name: nfo:depicts
symbols.summary: Relates an image to the information elements it depicts.

symbols.name: nfo:duration
symbols.summary: Duration of a media piece, measured in seconds.

symbols.name: nfo:encodedBy
symbols.summary: The contains the name of the person or organisation that encoded the media

symbols.name: nfo:encoding
symbols.summary: The encoding used for the Embedded File. Examples might include BASE64 or UUEncode

symbols.name: nfo:entryCounter
symbols.summary: Number of entries in the list. Optimize some common queries

symbols.name: nfo:entryUrl
symbols.summary: URL to the element in certain position of the list

symbols.name: nfo:equipment

symbols.name: nfo:equipmentSoftware

symbols.summary: File creation date

symbols.name: nfo:fileLastAccessed
symbols.summary: Time when the file was last accessed.

symbols.name: nfo:fileLastModified

symbols.name: nfo:fileName
symbols.summary: Name of the file, together with the extension

symbols.name: nfo:fileOwner
symbols.summary: The owner of the file as defined by the file system access rights feature.

symbols.name: nfo:fileSize
symbols.summary: The size of the file in bytes. For compressed files it means the size of the packed file, not of the contents. For folders it means the aggregated size of all contained files and folders

symbols.name: nfo:fontFamily
symbols.summary: The name of the font family.

symbols.name: nfo:foundry
symbols.summary: The foundry, the organization that created the font.

symbols.name: nfo:frameCount
symbols.summary: The amount of frames in a video sequence.

symbols.name: nfo:frameRate
symbols.summary: Amount of video frames per second.

symbols.name: nfo:frontChannels
symbols.summary: Number of front channels.

symbols.name: nfo:gain
symbols.summary: Gain of media

symbols.name: nfo:genre
symbols.summary: Genre of media

symbols.name: nfo:hasHash

symbols.name: nfo:hasMediaFileListEntry
symbols.summary: This property is intended to point to an RDF list of MediaFiles.

symbols.name: nfo:hasMediaStream
symbols.summary: Connects a media container with a single media stream contained within.

symbols.name: nfo:hasRegionOfInterest
symbols.summary: Link an element with a defined region

symbols.name: nfo:hashAlgorithm
symbols.summary: Name of the algorithm used to compute the hash value. Examples might include CRC32, MD5, SHA, TTH etc.

symbols.name: nfo:hashValue
symbols.summary: The actual value of the hash.

symbols.name: nfo:heading
symbols.summary: Specifies the direction of travelling while capturing image/video. The range of values from 0.00 to 359.99 (where 0 is due North, 90 is East, 180 South and 270 is West)

symbols.name: nfo:height

symbols.name: nfo:horizontalResolution

symbols.name: nfo:interlaceMode

symbols.name: nfo:isBootable

symbols.name: nfo:isContentEncrypted

symbols.name: nfo:isPasswordProtected

symbols.name: nfo:lastPlayedPosition
symbols.summary: Position in the media (in seconds) where the play was paused. Positive number, being 0 the beginning of the media.

symbols.name: nfo:lfeChannels
symbols.summary: Number of Low Frequency Expansion (subwoofer) channels.

symbols.name: nfo:lineCount
symbols.summary: The amount of lines in a text document

symbols.name: nfo:listDuration
symbols.summary: Sum of the duration of all items in the list. Optimize some common queries. In seconds

symbols.name: nfo:listPosition
symbols.summary: Position of an entry in a list. Double, to optimize the poor insertions

symbols.name: nfo:manufacturer
symbols.summary: The manufacturer of the equipment

symbols.name: nfo:mediaListEntry
symbols.summary: A certain item belongs to a media list. This can reflect that a song is in a playlist, an image or video in an Album

symbols.name: nfo:model
symbols.summary: The model of the equipment

symbols.name: nfo:originalLocation
symbols.summary: The original location of the deleted resource.

symbols.name: nfo:pageCount
symbols.summary: Number of pages.

symbols.name: nfo:pageNumber
symbols.summary: Page linked by the bookmark

symbols.name: nfo:peakGain
symbols.summary: Peak Gain of media

symbols.name: nfo:permissions
symbols.summary: A string containing the permissions of a file. A feature common in many UNIX-like operating systems.

symbols.name: nfo:programmingLanguage
symbols.summary: Indicates the name of the programming language this source code file is written in. Examples might include 'C', 'C++', 'Java' etc

symbols.name: nfo:rearChannels
symbols.summary: Number of rear channels.

symbols.name: nfo:regionOfInterestHeight
symbols.summary: Height of the region. It is normalized (values between 0 and 1) to the total height of the picture.

symbols.name: nfo:regionOfInterestType
symbols.summary: The content of a region can be one of the predefined types in the spec

symbols.name: nfo:regionOfInterestWidth
symbols.summary: Width of the region. It is normalized (values between 0 and 1) to the total width of the picture.

symbols.name: nfo:regionOfInterestX
symbols.summary: Coordinate X where the region starts. It is normalized (values between 0 and 1) to the width of the picture. Starting in the upper left corner.

symbols.name: nfo:regionOfInterestY

symbols.name: nfo:roiRefersTo
symbols.summary: Link to an item that is represented in the region. The 'type' of the region can give a clue of what exact content is linked in this property

symbols.name: nfo:sampleCount
symbols.summary: The amount of samples in an audio clip.

symbols.name: nfo:sampleRate
symbols.summary: The amount of audio samples per second.

symbols.name: nfo:sideChannels
symbols.summary: Number of side channels

symbols.name: nfo:softwareCategoryIcon
symbols.summary: Icon of the software

symbols.name: nfo:softwareCmdLine
symbols.summary: Command to launch the software

symbols.name: nfo:softwareIcon
symbols.summary: Icon of the software

symbols.name: nfo:streamPosition
symbols.summary: Stream position of the bookmark, suitable for e.g. audio books. Expressed in milliseconds

symbols.name: nfo:supercedes

symbols.name: nfo:tableOfContents
symbols.summary: Section titles and figure descriptions of the document.

symbols.name: nfo:tilt
symbols.summary: Vertical inclination of the camera while capturing the image, in angles starting on 0 as horizontal, positive numbers pointing up, negative angles pointing down

symbols.name: nfo:uncompressedSize
symbols.summary: Uncompressed size of the content of a compressed file.

symbols.name: nfo:verticalResolution
symbols.summary: Vertical resolution of an Image (if printed). Expressed in DPI

symbols.name: nfo:width
symbols.summary: Visual content width in pixels.

symbols.name: nfo:wordCount

symbols.name: nie:DataObject
symbols.summary: A unit of data that is created, annotated and processed on the user desktop. It represents a native structure the user works with. The usage of the term 'native'	is important. It means that a DataObject can be directly mapped to a data structure maintained by a native application.	This may be a file, a set of files or a part of a file. The granularity depends on the user. This class is not intended to be instantiated by itself. Use more specific subclasses.

symbols.name: nie:DataSource
symbols.summary: A superclass for all entities from which DataObjects can be extracted. Each entity represents a native application or some other system that manages information that may be of interest to the user of the Semantic Desktop. Subclasses may include FileSystems, Mailboxes, Calendars, websites etc. The exact choice of subclasses and their properties is considered application-specific. Each data extraction application is supposed to provide it's own DataSource ontology. Such an ontology should contain supported data source types coupled with properties necessary for the application to gain access to the data sources. (paths, urls, passwords etc...)

symbols.name: nie:InformationElement
symbols.summary: A unit of content the user works with. This is a superclass for all interpretations of a DataObject.

symbols.name: nie:byteSize
symbols.summary: File size in bytes

symbols.name: nie:characterSet
symbols.summary: Characterset in which the content of the InformationElement was created. Example: ISO-8859-1, UTF-8. One of the registered character sets at http://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets. This characterSet is used to interpret any textual parts of the content. If more than one characterSet is used within one data object, use more specific properties

symbols.name: nie:comment
symbols.summary: A user comment about an InformationElement

symbols.name: nie:contentCreated
symbols.summary: The date of the content creation. This may not necessarily be equal to the date when the DataObject (i.e. the physical representation) itself was created. Compare with nie:created property

symbols.name: nie:contentLastModified
symbols.summary: The date of the last modification of the original content (not its corresponding DataObject or local copy). Compare with nie:lastModified

symbols.name: nie:contentSize
symbols.summary: The size of the content. This property can be used whenever the size of the content of an InformationElement differs from the size of the DataObject. (e.g. because of compression, encoding, encryption or any other representation issues). The contentSize in expressed in bytes

symbols.name: nie:copyright
symbols.summary: Content copyright

symbols.name: nie:created
symbols.summary: Date of creation of the DataObject. Note that this date refers to the creation of the DataObject itself (i.e. the physical representation). Compare with nie:contentCreated

symbols.name: nie:dataSource
symbols.summary: Marks the provenance of a DataObject, what source does a data object come from

symbols.name: nie:depends
symbols.summary: Dependency relation. A piece of content depends on another piece of data in order to be properly understood/used/interpreted

symbols.name: nie:description
symbols.summary: A textual description of the resource. This property may be used for any metadata fields that provide some meta-information or comment about a resource in the form of a passage of text. This property is not to be confused with nie:plainTextContent. Use more specific subproperties wherever possible

symbols.name: nie:disclaimer
symbols.summary: A disclaimer

symbols.name: nie:generator
symbols.summary: Software used to 'generate' the contents. E.g. a word processor name

symbols.name: nie:hasLogicalPart
symbols.summary: Generic property used to express 'logical' containment relationships between InformationElements. NIE extensions are encouraged to provide more specific subproperties of this one. It is advisable for actual instances of InformationElement to use those specific subproperties. Note the difference between 'physical' containment (hasPart) and logical containment (hasLogicalPart)

symbols.name: nie:hasPart
symbols.summary: Generic property used to express 'physical' containment relationships between DataObjects. NIE extensions are encouraged to provide more specific subproperties of this one. It is advisable for actual instances of DataObjects to use those specific subproperties. Note to the developers: Please be aware of the distinction between containment relation and provenance. The hasPart relation models physical containment, an InformationElement (a nmo:Message) can have a 'physical' part (an nfo:Attachment). Also, please note the difference between physical containment (hasPart) and logical containment (hasLogicalPart) the former has more strict meaning. They may occur independently of each other

symbols.name: nie:identifier
symbols.summary: An unambiguous reference to the InformationElement within a given context. Recommended best practice is to identify the resource by means of a string conforming to a formal identification system

symbols.name: nie:informationElementDate
symbols.summary: A point or period of time associated with an event in the lifecycle of an Information Element. A common superproperty for all date-related properties of InformationElements in the NIE Framework

symbols.name: nie:interpretedAs
symbols.summary: Links the DataObject with the InformationElement it is interpreted as

symbols.name: nie:isLogicalPartOf
symbols.summary: Generic property used to express 'logical' containment relationships between DataObjects. NIE extensions are encouraged to provide more specific subproperties of this one. It is advisable for actual instances of InformationElement to use those specific subproperties. Note the difference between 'physical' containment (isPartOf) and logical containment (isLogicalPartOf)

symbols.name: nie:isPartOf
symbols.summary: Generic property used to express containment relationships between DataObjects. NIE extensions are encouraged to provide more specific subproperties of this one. It is advisable for actual instances of DataObjects to use those specific subproperties. Note to the developers: Please be aware of the distinction between containment relation and provenance. The isPartOf relation models physical containment, a nie:DataObject (e.g. an nfo:Attachment) is a 'physical' part of an nie:InformationElement (a nmo:Message). Also, please note the difference between physical containment (isPartOf) and logical containment (isLogicalPartOf) the former has more strict meaning. They may occur independently of each other

symbols.name: nie:isStoredAs
symbols.summary: Links the information element with the DataObject it is stored in

symbols.name: nie:keyword
symbols.summary: Adapted DublinCore: The topic of the content of the resource, as keyword. No sentences here. Recommended best practice is to select a value from a controlled vocabulary or formal classification scheme

symbols.name: nie:language
symbols.summary: Language the InformationElement is expressed in. Users are encouraged to use the two-letter code specified in the RFC 3066

symbols.name: nie:lastRefreshed
symbols.summary: Date when information about this data object was retrieved (for the first time) or last refreshed from the data source. This property is important for metadata extraction applications that don't receive any notifications of changes in the data source and have to poll it regularly. This may lead to information becoming out of date. In these cases this property may be used to determine the age of data, which is an important element of it's dependability

symbols.name: nie:legal
symbols.summary: A common superproperty for all properties that point at legal information about an Information Element

symbols.name: nie:license
symbols.summary: Terms and intellectual property rights licensing conditions.

symbols.name: nie:licenseType
symbols.summary: The type of the license. Possible values for this field may include 'GPL', 'BSD', 'Creative Commons' etc.

symbols.name: nie:links
symbols.summary: A linking relation. A piece of content links/mentions a piece of data

symbols.name: nie:mimeType
symbols.summary: File Mime Type

symbols.name: nie:plainTextContent
symbols.summary: Plain-text representation of the content of a InformationElement with all markup removed. The main purpose of this property is full-text indexing and search. Its exact content is considered application-specific. The user can make no assumptions about what is and what is not contained within. Applications should use more specific properties wherever possible.

symbols.name: nie:relatedTo
symbols.summary: A common superproperty for all relations between a piece of content and other pieces of data (which may be interpreted as other pieces of content).

symbols.name: nie:rootElementOf
symbols.summary: DataObjects extracted from a single data source are organized into a containment tree. This property links the root of that tree with the datasource it has been extracted from

symbols.name: nie:subject
symbols.summary: The subject or topic of the document

symbols.name: nie:title
symbols.summary: The title of the document

symbols.name: nie:url
symbols.summary: URL pointing at the location of the resource. In cases where creating a simple file:// or http:// URL for a file is difficult (e.g. for files inside compressed archives) the applications are encouraged to use conventions defined by Apache Commons VFS Project at http://jakarta.apache.org/  commons/ vfs/ filesystems.html.

symbols.name: nie:version
symbols.summary: The current version of the given data object. Exact semantics is unspecified at this level. Use more specific subproperties if needed
